forecasts.question: Will Iran and Oman jointly announce a formal Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor arrangement before EOD 2026-08-08?
forecasts.delta_reason: Aug 6: Iran-Oman joint communiqué published on Oman FM website (fm.gov.om) and confirmed by Iran MFA spokesman Baghaei. Bilateral publication criterion satisfied. Communiqué covers: (a) agreement on geographic route coordinates for a navigable channel; (b) establishment of joint working group to determine 'future administration of navigation, services and costs.' No service fees, per-vessel charges, or named transit costs appear in published text. Baghaei explicitly described fee structure as deferred to working group. Ambiguity rule triggered: 'Service-fee outline without formal named agreement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.' Resolved AMBIGUOUS, treated as NO. Successor: F8.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if both Iran's Foreign Ministry and Oman's Foreign Ministry publicly announce, or a formal joint communiqué is issued, confirming a Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor arrangement that specifies at minimum (a) the corridor route or geographic parameters, and (b) either a fee structure or a confirmed no-fee arrangement, before EOD 2026-08-08.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IRNA or Oman News Agency (ONA) announcing the framework, confirmed by one TIER1 source (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera). Either government's unilateral announcement independently confirmed by TIER1 also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Araghchi or Omani FM stating talks are in 'final stages' or 'nearing conclusion' without a formal announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A framework that leaves fee structure, route, or effective date as TBD = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. US government acceptance or opposition does NOT affect resolution — this forecast measures the Iran-Oman bilateral announcement only.

forecasts.question: Will the United States military conduct confirmed new strikes against targets on Iranian soil before EOD 2026-08-11?
forecasts.delta_reason: No US strikes on Iranian sovereign territory Aug 4-6. Trump cancelled planned air campaign Aug 1 (confirmed: Axios/NPR/WaPo/CBS) — sixth consecutive night of post-cancellation pause. Bessent Aug 4-5 deal deadlines elapsed without strike or agreement. Iran Aug 6 stated US is 'ready to return to commitments' under June 17 MOU, consistent with active backchannel communication. Five days remain on Aug 11 horizon. DA p=0.07 judged too low — prior cancellations have been reversed and residual probability for remaining window is non-trivial given Trump's documented reversal pattern. p moved 0.24 → 0.12.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Pentagon or CENTCOM confirms airstrikes, missile strikes, or special-operations raids conducted by US forces against targets located within Iran's internationally recognized land borders before EOD 2026-08-11. Strikes against Iranian naval vessels or IRGC-directed proxies in Iraq, Syria, Yemen, or at sea do NOT qualify.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Pentagon or CENTCOM official statement (press release on defense.gov or war.gov) confirming strikes on Iranian soil, OR Reuters/AP/AFP with named US Department of Defense or CENTCOM official confirmation.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump public threat or warning without confirmed execution = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Strikes against Iranian proxies in third countries do not count. If target location on Iranian soil is disputed by both sides, default to NO. US strikes against Iranian vessels at sea = NO.

forecasts.question: Will a formal US-Iran negotiating session — direct or mediated by a named state mediator — be confirmed by both parties before EOD 2026-08-18?
forecasts.delta_reason: Iran MFA Aug 6 sustained Aug 3 denial: 'path of understanding is between Iran and Oman.' New element introduced: Iran characterized US as 'ready to return to commitments' under June 17 MOU — Iran's framing of US posture, not confirmation of a direct session. Qatar FM described broader process as in 'very progressive stages.' Iran-Oman joint working group creates documented bilateral institutional channel. Twelve days remain. Iran's sustained denial is dispositive against higher values; active Oman channel and documented working group are dispositive against lower values. p moved 0.26 → 0.22.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Reuters or AP reports — with named spokespeople or officials from both the US and Iran — that a face-to-face negotiating session (direct, or third-country mediated by Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, or another named state) was held between named US and Iranian government principals or envoys before EOD 2026-08-18. The Oman-Iran Hormuz corridor track alone does NOT qualify unless the US is formally a named party to the session.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP carrying confirmation from both a named US government representative (State Dept, NSA, CENTCOM, or designated envoy) AND a named Iranian government representative (MFA official or designated envoy). One-sided confirmation from the US side alone = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump assertion without Iranian MFA confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Oman-Iran bilateral session without US participation = does NOT count. Written message exchanges or intermediary-relayed communications without a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. 'Talks about talks' or preparatory meetings without substantive negotiation do NOT count.

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping transits through the Strait of Hormuz reach ≥30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average, IMF PortWatch) before EOD 2026-09-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: Kpler/AIS Jul 27-Aug 2: 106 all-vessel Hormuz crossings (96 distinct vessels, ~15/day) — all-vessel figure, NOT commercial-transit count. TankerMap Aug 5: 0 tanker transits (against 7-day all-vessel avg ~1/day). Dark AIS 41%. P&I war-risk cover suspended. Pre-crisis commercial baseline ~100/day. Aug 6 corridor communiqué establishes route coordinates but names no fees; insurance normalization and shipper-confidence recovery have not occurred. Resolution criterion requires 30 commercial transits/day 7-day rolling average — structural normalization well beyond current paper agreement. 32 days remain. p moved 0.20 → 0.08. Note: Kpler ~15/day is all-vessel; TankerMap 0 tankers is resolution-relevant commercial-transit metric.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch records a 7-day rolling average of ≥30 commercial vessel transits per day through the Strait of Hormuz in any consecutive 7-day window with the final day falling before EOD 2026-09-07.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch public dashboard (portwatch.imf.org) as primary source. If PortWatch is temporarily unavailable, Lloyd's List Intelligence or Bloomberg shipping-data report may substitute; flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict by >20%. Single-day figures do not resolve; the full 7-day rolling average is required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Single-day spikes above 30 without a qualifying 7-day rolling average = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Naval-escorted convoys count toward transit total. If PortWatch data is unavailable for more than 3 consecutive days within the window, extend horizon by equivalent days and flag AMBIGUOUS until data restored.

indicators.name: IMF PortWatch 7-day rolling average rises above 20/day (leading indicator threshold)
P&I war-risk insurance reinstated for Hormuz transit by Lloyd's or equivalent

forecasts.question: Will Iran agree to a verified freeze or transfer of its highly enriched uranium (≥60% enriched) stockpile as part of a binding framework before EOD 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. IAEA lacks access to Isfahan underground HEU storage. June 2026 Switzerland talks established four working groups including Nuclear Affairs but no HEU freeze mechanism confirmed. Iran ballistic missile program characterized as 'not for negotiation.' Diplomatic focus entirely on Hormuz corridor. p=0.13 unchanged.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Iran officially agrees — in a written document cosigned or formally witnessed by the IAEA or a named state guarantor — to either (a) a verified freeze of its ≥60% enriched UF6 stockpile at or below the August 4, 2026 IAEA-confirmed level, with continuous IAEA monitoring, or (b) transfer of its ≥60% enriched UF6 stockpile to a named third country, before EOD 2026-10-27.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA Director General's written report or official press statement confirming the arrangement as primary source, plus Reuters/AP confirmation. IRNA (Iran state media) acknowledging the agreement alongside IAEA confirmation also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Verbal commitment to future freeze without a signed, witnessed document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Framework reducing new enrichment rates but not addressing the existing stockpile = does NOT count. Provisional or temporary halt without IAEA continuous monitoring = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Trump or Iranian FM assertion of 'agreement in principle' without IAEA confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Iran and US or P3+1 announce binding framework document witnessed by IAEA

forecasts.question: Will a right-wing bloc led by Netanyahu's Likud win ≥61 Knesset seats in Israel's October 27, 2026 legislative election?
forecasts.delta_reason: Channel 12 Aug 4 poll: Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar each at 23 seats; right bloc total ~50, eleven seats short of 61-seat threshold. JPost Aug 4: Eisenkot leads Netanyahu by 10 points in PM preference; Beyachad (Bennett-Lapid) at 26. Consistent right-bloc aggregate ~50 across multiple August polls. No electoral pact or merger announced. 82 days to October 27 election allow some polling movement but 11-seat gap is structural. p moved 0.22 → 0.13.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, in the Israeli Knesset election of October 27, 2026, the combined certified seat total of all right-wing parties publicly committing to support a Netanyahu-led government reaches ≥61 seats in the final certified results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee before EOD 2026-11-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official certified results, carried by Reuters/AP/Times of Israel/Haaretz. Exit polls alone do not resolve; certified count required.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary exit polls or election-night projections without certified final count = AMBIGUOUS pending certification. If recount is in progress at EOD 2026-11-15, extend horizon by 7 days and maintain OPEN-AMBIGUOUS status. If no Netanyahu-led government is attempted despite ≥61 right-wing seats, resolve YES based on seat count alone. Parties committing to a non-Netanyahu right-wing PM do not count toward the 61.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: No formal Knesset roll-call majority-loss vote confirmed. Knesset dissolved July 17 via consensual 62-0 vote — Haredi MKs voted with coalition to dissolve, not against it. JPost 'coalition falls to 48 seats' is polling projection for October 27 election, not actual coalition composition. i24NEWS 'coalition majority dissolved' describes operational Haredi legislative boycott, not a formal majority-loss event. October 27 election date unchanged — not earlier than resolution threshold. Both YES criteria structurally foreclosed. p=0.06 retained.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (below 61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact through dissolution.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas. Orderly end-of-term dissolution with election fixed at or after Oct 27 = RESOLVE-NO at horizon.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and Oman formally publish an operational Strait of Hormuz transit framework — including named service fees or a defined per-vessel cost structure — before EOD 2026-08-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast; direct successor to resolved F1. Aug 6 Iran-Oman joint communiqué established a joint working group with explicit mandate to determine 'future administration of navigation, services and costs.' Working group is the documented institutional vehicle; both governments publicly committed to fee-determination process. 16-day horizon. Named fee framework within 16 days requires accelerated working-group output. Upward pressure: both governments committed, geographic route confirmed, Iranian domestic audience being prepared for a fee regime framed as 'sovereign rights.' Downward pressure: IRGC toll preference vs US rejection of any transit fee regime is a structural impasse; P&I cover and US Navy posture unchanged. p=0.38 reflects established institutional process against short horizon and structural complexity.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Iran-Oman joint working group, or either government on behalf of the bilateral arrangement, publicly releases a document naming specific service fees, per-vessel transit charges, or a defined cost schedule for commercial passage through the Strait of Hormuz — with both governments' endorsement confirmed — before EOD 2026-08-22.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/Al Jazeera) OR official state media (Oman ONA + Iran IRNA/Tasnim) carrying the published fee schedule. Both governments must confirm or co-publish the document.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Reference to fees 'to be determined' or 'in accordance with international standards' without published rates = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. US rejection does NOT affect resolution. Fee schedule covering only IRGC-supervised vessels without general commercial applicability = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Ambiguity rule applied: 'one side asserting talks continue without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.' forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. IMF PortWatch 7-day average reached approximately 25 ships/day during the MOU period (late June-early July) — well below the 50/day threshold. Single-day peaks of approximately 51-52 on June 24-25 do not satisfy the 7-day rolling average criterion per ambiguity rule ('one-off surge days do NOT qualify'). After July 6-7 Iranian attacks on commercial vessels, any brief recovery reversed and traffic fell to approximately 10/day. No 7-day window before EOD July 2 recorded ≥50 transits/day.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. CENTCOM press release on DOD/war.gov: 'US Forces Start Mine Clearance Mission in Strait of Hormuz,' dated approximately June 16 — within the June 10-July 10 resolution window. CENTCOM press release constitutes a 'named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement' under the resolution source rule; as a DOD primary source it is authoritative without requiring TIER1 relay. Corroborated by DefenseScoop, Naval News, Army Recognition. UK (RFA Lyme Bay) and French minehunters arrived in early July. Källa A's failure to locate TIER1 coverage reflects a research gap; the CENTCOM primary source is determinative. The mission's subsequent disruption by the July 7 conflict resumption does not affect the resolution (commencement within window is the criterion). final_p=0.82 reflects high confidence in YES with slight discount for the absence of TIER1 carry.
